title: AICONTROL1: How much control do you think you have in whether AI is used in your life? (American Trends Panel)
measure: % of US adults saying 'not too much' or 'none' control over whether AI is used in their life
finding: Not too much or no control: 59% (2024) then 57% (2025); 'not too much' 41% to 40%, 'none' 18% to 17%; change within noise.
limits: two cross-sections; about AI use in own life, not political say; no 2026 reading found

title: AICONTROL2: Comfortable with control vs would like more control over how AI is used in my life
measure: % of US adults who would like more control over how AI is used in their life
finding: Wanting more control rose 6 points (55% to 61%) while 'not sure' fell 26% to 21%; comfortable 19% to 17%.
limits: two readings; desire for control is not loss of influence

title: More concerned than excited about increased use of AI in daily life (short read, Aug 2026)
measure: % of US adults more concerned than excited about AI
finding: Concern rose from 37% (2021) to 52% (2026); ages 18-29 from 31% to 55%; this short read has no control item.
limits: mood, not say; confirms no 2026 control reading in this release

title: US public and AI experts: government will go too far vs not far enough regulating AI; confidence in government and companies
measure: % more concerned US government will not go far enough (vs too far) regulating AI; % with not too much/no confidence in government to regulate AI
latest_value: 58% not far enough vs 21% too far (Aug 2024, n=5,410); 62% not too much/no confidence in government to regulate; 59% in companies
finding: Most Americans wanted more AI regulation than they expected to get (58% vs 21%) and few trusted either government (29% at least some confidence) or companies (32%).
limits: one reading; not repeated in Pew's Jun 2025 topline

title: Americans Prioritize AI Safety and Data Security
measure: % of US adults favouring government AI safety and data-security rules even if AI develops more slowly
finding: 80% favour keeping safety rules even if AI develops more slowly, 9% favour speed; 54% say the US government should make AI rules, 3% want none.
limits: one reading; measures preference, not whether it is acted on

cite: Ada Lovelace Institute & Alan Turing Institute 2025
title: How do people feel about AI? (second wave; Public Voices in AI)
measure: % of UK adults saying laws and regulation would increase comfort with AI; % not feeling their views are represented in current AI decisions
latest_value: 72% laws would increase comfort (2025) vs 62% (2022/23); 50% do not feel represented (2025), n=3,513
finding: Half of UK adults say their views and values are not represented in current AI decisions; demand for laws rose 10 points since 2022/23.
limits: representation item seen for one wave only; fieldwork dates not on page

title: Trust, attitudes and use of AI: a global study 2025
measure: % of adults across 47 countries who believe AI regulation is needed
finding: 70% across 47 countries say AI regulation is needed.
limits: consultancy co-funded; earlier wave comparison not read; preference not influence

cite: YouGov / Institute for Family Studies 2025 (via Public Citizen memo)
title: Federal preemption of state AI laws (NDAA)
measure: % of US adults opposing vs supporting federal preemption of state AI laws
finding: As reported by an advocacy compilation, opposition to blocking state AI laws outran support about 3 to 1, a month before the federal executive order targeting state AI laws.
limits: read only in an advocacy compilation; original poll not read

title: AI Polling Memo (17 Sep 2026): compilation of 39 US polls on AI
measure: compilation of poll toplines on AI regulation, preemption, data centres and trust
latest_value: e.g. AIPI Jun 2026: 78% prefer mandatory safety standards; NBC Aug 2026: 69% oppose a local AI data centre
finding: Across 39 polls from 2021 to 2026, large majorities favour more AI regulation and oppose local data centres and federal preemption.
limits: advocacy compilation; mixes question wordings; no fieldwork dates or n

cite: AlgoSoc AI Opinion Monitor (University of Amsterdam) 2024-2026
title: AI Opinion Monitor / Longitudinal Effects Panel (LISS)
measure: agreement with 'I know how I can influence what content is recommended to me by AI'; trust in automated decisions
latest_value: 5 waves Mar 2024 to May 2026, about 4,000 adults each; values not read
finding: Same Dutch adults asked repeatedly whether they know how to influence AI recommendations; no values read in this search.
limits: one country; values not retrieved

title: Global Dialogues
measure: recurring 'Global Pulse Indicators' (trust, AI usage, future outlook) from about 1,000 people per round
latest_value: 9 rounds Nov 2024-May 2026; May 2026: 1,024 people, 69 countries; indicator values not read
finding: A repeated multi-country deliberative survey on AI exists; question wording and values for trust and say were not visible on its page.
limits: online opt-in-style samples (repIndex 73%); values not read

title: Public Trust in Government: 1958-2025
measure: % trusting the government in Washington to do what is right just about always or most of the time
finding: Trust fell from 77% (1964) to about 25% by 1980 and has not exceeded 30% since 2007; 17% in 2025.
limits: not tied to AI; decline long predates AI; mode changes over time

title: Trust and confidence in Britain's system of government at record low
measure: % trusting governments to put the needs of the nation above party interests just about always or most of the time
finding: Trust in governments to put the nation first fell to a record low of 12% in 2024; 19% say the system needs little or no improvement.
limits: not tied to AI; read via trade press, not NatCen's page; first year is the survey's start as reported; item start not checked

title: Political efficacy: 'the political system allows people like you to have a say in what the government does'
measure: 5-point agreement that the system allows people like you a say
finding: Repeated cross-national baseline for perceived political say; no AI item alongside it was found.
limits: biennial; not tied to AI; trend values not read

title: External efficacy: 'People like me don't have any say about what the government does'
measure: % agreeing people like me have no say (election years)
finding: Long-run US series on perceived say; values for 2020 and 2024 not read in this search.
limits: every 4 years; not tied to AI

title: 'People like me don't have any say in what the government does' (waves 3, 6, 12)
measure: agreement that people like me have no say, same people across waves
finding: A same-people panel item on political say exists; AI-use items alongside it were not confirmed.
limits: irregular waves; not tied to AI

title: Democracy Report 2026: Unraveling the Democratic Era?
measure: expert-coded Liberal Democracy Index (0-1); share of world population in autocracies
latest_value: 74% of world population in autocracies (2025 data); average citizen back to 1978 level; US LDI -0.218 since 2023
finding: Democracy for the average person is back to 1978 levels, 44 countries are autocratising and the US lost liberal-democracy status; the report does not mention AI.
limits: context only; drivers are political, not AI

title: Freedom on the Net 2025: The Uncertain Future of the Global Internet
measure: internet freedom scores, 72 countries; narrative cases of AI-generated political content
latest_value: 15th consecutive year of decline; 28 of 72 countries declined, 17 improved
finding: Internet freedom fell for a 15th year; AI cases (Ghana bot network, India-Pakistan AI content) are anecdotes with no count.
limits: AI not separated from other causes; no AI count in 2025

title: Freedom on the Net 2023: The Repressive Power of Artificial Intelligence
measure: number of countries where AI tools were used to distort information; countries mandating automated censorship
latest_value: at least 16 countries (generative AI to sow doubt or smear); 21-22 countries mandating automated censorship (Jun 2022-May 2023)
finding: AI tools were used in at least 16 countries to sow doubt, smear opponents or sway debate; the count was not repeated in 2025.
limits: one-off count; page gives both 21 and 22

title: Monthly Budget Review: September 2026 (fiscal year 2026, preliminary)
measure: individual income + payroll taxes as % of federal receipts (derived from CBO $bn)
finding: The share rose about 2 points to 86.2% in FY2026 as corporate receipts fell 16% (2025 reconciliation act) and about $130bn of IEEPA tariffs were refunded.
limits: preliminary; derived; moves with tax policy; income tax includes capital gains

title: Revenue Statistics 2025 (special feature: disentangling personal income tax revenue)
measure: tax structure shares (PIT, social contributions, payroll, corporate, consumption) of total tax revenue, OECD countries
finding: A multi-country annual series on how much revenue comes from labour-related taxes exists, and the 2025 edition splits personal income tax by income source; figures not read.
limits: figures not retrieved; not tied to AI

title: Generative Influence: AI lobbying 2020-2025
measure: lobbyists whose federal disclosures mention AI (or AV, data centres) as % of all federal lobbyists (OpenSecrets totals)
finding: The share of federal lobbyists working on AI rose from 10-11% (2020-22) to 26% (2025), and AI lobbying clients more than tripled.
limits: advocacy analysis; keyword match includes AV, data centres, facial recognition and non-industry clients; effort, not success

title: AI interest groups pour tens of millions of dollars into 2026 election
measure: super PAC money from AI interests (FEC filings), races targeted
latest_value: Leading the Future: $125m reported from Brockman, Andreessen, Horowitz and others; 36 races; Think Big >$8m against Alex Bores (lost); Public First Action $80m, about half from Anthropic (Sep 2026)
finding: An AI-industry super PAC network reported $125m in backing and spent in 36 races; its top target, a state AI-safety legislator, lost his primary.
limits: secondary report; one cycle; whether spending caused outcomes is untested

title: Pro-AI super PAC keeps $31M ready for the midterms
measure: cash on hand and transfers of AI super PACs, Q2 2026
latest_value: Leading the Future ~$31m cash (end Q2 2026), $20m moved to affiliates; Public First PAC raised ~$3.4m in Q2; Anthropic gave $20m to Public First Action
finding: The pro-industry PAC network held about $31m in cash mid-2026, more than ten times the combined PAC cash reported for the AI-safety side (its nonprofit funds are not comparable).
limits: secondary; cash on hand is not spending; nonprofit money not fully disclosed

title: Artificial Intelligence 2025 Legislation
measure: number of states introducing and enacting AI legislation per year
latest_value: all 50 states introduced; 38 states adopted or enacted about 100 measures (as of 10 Jul 2025)
finding: Every state introduced AI bills in 2025 and 38 enacted about 100 measures, so legislatures are acting on AI.
limits: counts bills, not their strength; mid-year snapshot

title: Data Center Watch quarterly reports
measure: value ($bn) and number of US data-centre projects blocked or delayed by local opposition
latest_value: Q1 2026: at least 75 projects, ~$130bn; Q2 2026: at least 45 projects, ~$68bn; 2025: $152-156bn
finding: Local opposition blocked or delayed about $130bn of data-centre projects in Q1 2026 alone, roughly the whole of 2025.
limits: methodology not published; periods differ between reports; minimum estimates

title: Reported milestones for AI in government (firsts)
measure: count of reported first uses or symbolic delegations of AI in lawmaking, administration, justice and military
finding: Events, not a series; several are stated goals or symbolic appointments.
limits: selection by news coverage

title: DOGE builds AI tool to cut 50 percent of federal regulations
measure: reported use of an AI tool to decide which federal regulations to cut
latest_value: 'decisions on 1,083 regulatory sections' at HUD in under two weeks; '100% of deregulations' written at CFPB (Jul 2025, per internal slides)
finding: Internal slides described a mostly automated AI tool meant to flag about 100,000 of 200,000 federal rules for cutting; HUD said no decisions were completed.
limits: leaked slides; agency disputes; outcome not tracked

title: UAE launches 32 AI Cabinet advisers to support government decision-making
measure: reported deployment of AI advisers to a national cabinet
finding: The UAE Cabinet deployed 32 AI assistants to analyse policy and follow up decisions; the role is described as advisory.
limits: announcement; no evidence on decisions changed

title: Alberta minister reportedly putting together first AI-generated legislation in Canada
measure: reported plan to draft a bill (Alberta Whisky Act) with AI
finding: Alberta's Service Alberta minister said an AI-drafted bill, vetted by officials, would be a first in Canada.
limits: small outlet; original source not named; introduction not confirmed

title: Executive Order 'Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence' (11 Dec 2025)
measure: federal action against state AI laws; Senate vote on moratorium
latest_value: Senate removed 10-year state-law moratorium 99-1 (mid-2025); EO of 11 Dec 2025 creates DOJ AI Litigation Task Force and ties BEAD funds
finding: After the Senate rejected a moratorium 99-1, the executive branch moved to challenge state AI laws through litigation and funding conditions, while polls compiled by an advocacy group show majorities opposed preemption.
limits: law-firm summary; outcome of litigation not tracked

title: Persuading voters using human-artificial intelligence dialogues (Nature 648:394-401)
measure: change in candidate preference after a conversation with an AI advocating one candidate
finding: Pre-registered experiments in the US 2024, Canada 2025 and Poland 2025 elections found AI dialogues shifted candidate preference more than typical video ads; pro-right AIs made more inaccurate claims.
limits: online samples; stated preference; persistence in SI not read

title: The levers of political persuasion with conversational artificial intelligence (Science)
measure: attitude change on 707 political issues across 19 LLMs (n=76,977)
finding: Post-training and prompting raised persuasion more than scale or personalisation, with less accurate claims; 36-42% of the effect remained at one month.
limits: covered in landscape beliefs pass; not re-read this session

cite: Stockwell et al. (CETaS, Alan Turing Institute) 2024
title: AI-Enabled Influence Operations: Safeguarding Future Elections
measure: catalogued viral AI-enabled election content and assessed impact on results
finding: No evidence that AI-enabled disinformation measurably altered any 2024 election result tracked (US, UK, EU, Taiwan, India), largely because data on voter behaviour are lacking.
limits: absence of evidence; case catalogue (about 55 instances by our sum)

title: Testing Theories of American Politics: Elites, Interest Groups, and Average Citizens
measure: association of policy outcomes with preferences of average citizens, economic elites and interest groups (1,779 issues)
finding: Economic elites and business groups had substantial independent influence on US policy; average citizens had little or none, decades before generative AI.
limits: contested method; pre-AI baseline

title: When Do the Rich Win? (Political Science Quarterly 132(1))
measure: how often policy matches the rich vs the middle class when they disagree
finding: Re-analysis of Gilens' data finds the rich win somewhat more often when groups disagree, but groups mostly agree, so the middle class usually gets what it wants.
limits: not re-read this session; link not checked

title: AI can help humans find common ground in democratic deliberation (Science)
measure: ratings of AI-mediated group statements; within-group division (n=5,734 plus a virtual citizens' assembly)
finding: LLM-drafted group statements were preferred to human mediators' and reduced division while keeping dissent.
limits: Google DeepMind authors; short online sessions; covered in landscape group pass

cite: EPFL AI Center, Uni Geneva & Demoscan 2026
title: 'AI, good servant, bad master': citizens' assembly on AI (French-speaking Switzerland)
measure: recommendations from 40 randomly selected residents
finding: A 40-person assembly produced 20 proposals (including a federal AI office and labelling of human-made content); no body committed to respond.
limits: one-off; advisory only

title: Governing the Future: Recommendations from the Edinburgh Data and AI Exchange
measure: recommendations from a 99-person stakeholder assembly
finding: Recommends a standing, resourced UK citizens' assembly on AI; no government response reported.
limits: stakeholders, not random citizens; one-off

title: I checked out one of the biggest anti-AI protests yet
measure: size and demands of street protest against AI
finding: London's 28 Feb 2026 march (Pause AI, Pull the Plug) drew 'a couple of hundred', up from a few dozen in June 2025.
limits: journalist estimate; no protest-count series found

title: Thousands of AI Authors on the Future of AI
measure: share of 2,778 AI researchers saying substantial or extreme concern is warranted about scenarios
finding: More than half said substantial or extreme concern is warranted about six scenarios including misinformation, authoritarian control and inequality.
limits: expert concern, not a forecast of influence; per-item figures not read

title: Public Finance in the Age of AI: A Primer (NBER w34873)
measure: theory of how AI erodes labour and consumption tax bases
finding: AI 'may gradually erode the two main tax bases' (labour, then consumption), so states may come to depend on taxing AI itself.
limits: model; no measured erosion

title: Gradual Disempowerment, s6.2 'Estimating Human Disempowerment'
measure: proposed system-specific metrics
finding: Proposes political metrics including 'the effectiveness of traditional democratic mechanisms in influencing outcomes', AI's role in policy formation, and AI's role in lobbying; no tax-base metric.
limits: proposals only

title: Measuring AI-Induced Disempowerment: A Framework and Proposed Metrics (EvalEval, ACL)
measure: six proposed metrics incl. disempowerment perception surveys and capital flow to labour
finding: Finds current work clusters at exposure; proposes perception surveys, capital-flow monitoring and four other metrics, none fielded.
limits: proposal

title: A Formal Model of How Artificial Intelligence Erodes Human Agency (RR-A4817-1)
measure: decisive-coalition distribution, minimal coalition size and composition
finding: Proposes tracking who sits in the smallest decisive group, human participation thresholds and reversibility benchmarks; no application to a real institution reported.
limits: theoretical
